documents.title: Generative AI Guidance
documents.summary: IT Services guidance on using and procuring generative AI tools. It is mostly about data protection, tool review and procurement. It sets no student AI-use stance and sends academic-integrity questions to the teaching center.
documents.stance_why: The page never says whether students may use AI in coursework. Its one academic-integrity item says only "it is recommended that instructors contact the Chicago Center for Teaching and Learning", so the decision is left to instructors; the rest is data security and procurement rules.

units.why: The opening says users "must consider issues related to information security, privacy, compliance, and academic integrity", an institution-level statement of the principles behind the guidance, so P56 rather than a specific rule type.
units.anchor: must consider issues related to information security, privacy, compliance, and academic integrity

units.why: The sentence names a benefit ("capabilities and efficiencies that can greatly enhance our work") with no rule attached, so it is a benefit statement (P87).
units.anchor: offer many capabilities and efficiencies that can greatly enhance our work

units.why: "prohibited without prior security and privacy review" bars confidential data in public tools unless reviewed, so it is a data-protection rule (P50) and a restriction rather than a total ban.
units.anchor: with publicly available generative AI tools is prohibited without prior security and privacy review

units.why: The sentence lists employee, FERPA and HIPAA data as confidential data, which defines what the data rule above covers; coded P50 because it says what data to protect.
units.anchor: personally identifiable employee data, FERPA-covered student data, HIPAA-covered patient data

units.why: Some grantors "have policies prohibiting the use of generative AI tools in analyzing or reviewing grant applications", a research and grant rule that defers to funder policy (P62).
units.anchor: prohibiting the use of generative AI tools in analyzing or reviewing grant applications

units.why: It warns that sharing information with public tools "may expose sensitive information to unauthorized parties or violate data use agreements", giving the reason for the data rule (P50).
units.anchor: may expose sensitive information to unauthorized parties or violate data use agreements

units.why: "AI-generated content may be misleading or inaccurate" and may cite content that does not exist: a warning that output is unreliable, matching P31.
units.anchor: AI-generated content may be misleading or inaccurate

units.why: "It is the responsibility of the tool user to review the accuracy and ownership" puts a duty on the user to verify output (P31). Ownership is not part of P31, so a fit note is given; P52 covers only that half.
units.anchor: responsibility of the tool user to review the accuracy and ownership of any AI-generated content
units.fit_note: Also requires review of ownership (copyright) of AI-generated content, not only accuracy.

units.why: The statement that responses "may be copyrighted" and contain other authors' material is a copyright warning, matching P52.
units.anchor: may contain content and materials from other authors and may be copyrighted

units.why: For academic honesty the page only says it is "recommended that instructors contact the Chicago Center for Teaching and Learning", handing the question elsewhere. P63 fits best because it points instructors to a teaching center; P04 does not fit since no instructor-set rule is stated.
units.anchor: it is recommended that instructors contact the Chicago Center for Teaching and Learning
units.fit_note: Also defers the whole academic-integrity question to the teaching center; the page sets no integrity rule itself.

units.why: "require a security review before they are acquired, even if the software is free" is a mandatory review of AI tools before acquisition, so P65.
units.anchor: require a security review before they are acquired, even if the software is free
units.frag_start: Generative AI systems, applications, and software

units.why: "submitting our Generative AI Tool Review form before acquiring or using any tools" sets a required pre-use review procedure, matching P65.
units.anchor: submitting our Generative AI Tool Review form before acquiring or using any tools

units.why: Users "should first review the approved tools and use cases", telling people to use the approved list, which is P92; "should" gives the modality.
units.anchor: should first review the approved tools and use cases
units.frag_start: Members of the University community who wish

units.why: The approved list is "updated bi-monthly with decisions approved by the University's Chief Technology Officer (CTO) and Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)", which names who decides, so P80.
units.anchor: decisions approved by the University's Chief Technology Officer (CTO) and Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)

units.why: Paid tools go through "ServiceNow Procurement Intake" and free tools through the evaluation form: a required review route for unlisted tools, P65.
units.anchor: individuals should submit a request through ServiceNow Procurement Intake
units.frag_start: For paid tools, individuals should submit
units.fit_note: Splits the route by paid versus free tools.

units.why: The forms "inform updates to the University's approved tools and use cases list", describing how the list is revised, so P54 is the nearest type but fits only partly.
units.anchor: helps inform updates to the University's approved tools and use cases list
units.fit_note: About updating the approved-tool list from review requests, not the whole policy.

units.why: Researchers using AI in human-subjects studies "must inform the Institutional Review Board", a research-use rule that defers to the IRB, matching P62.
units.anchor: must inform the Institutional Review Board (IRB)
units.frag_start: Researchers who wish to use AI tools

units.why: Review aims to "prevent inadvertent exposure of institutional data to external systems", stating the purpose of the tool review process (P65).
units.anchor: prevent inadvertent exposure of institutional data to external systems
units.frag_start: This level of detail is essential

units.why: The review criteria (research obligations, system impact, safeguards, business case) define how AI tools are evaluated before approval, so P65.
units.anchor: Information Assurance reviews generative AI tools to ensure they are used securely, responsibly

units.why: "Use of University data by vendors to train or improve their models is not permitted" limits sharing university data with AI providers, the core of P65.
units.anchor: Use of University data by vendors to train or improve their models is not permitted

units.why: "Requests involving elevated or unresolved risk are escalated to senior leadership for final determination" names who decides hard cases, so P80.
units.anchor: escalated to senior leadership for final determination

units.why: Pointing users to PhoenixAI, "the University's internal generative AI platform", names an institution-wide provided tool: P92 rather than P17, which is course-specific.
units.anchor: internal generative AI platform may now provide equivalent functionality

units.why: A Risk Acceptance Letter is a formal route to an exception when use "exceeds standard risk tolerance", so it names the exception process (P80).
units.anchor: Getting an exception through a Risk Acceptance Letter (RAL)

units.why: Paid versions carry "contractual assurances that institutional data will not be used for model training", explaining why tool choice matters for data protection (P50).
units.anchor: contractual assurances that institutional data will not be used for model training

units.why: "The tool must be purchased through Procurement" when the free version lacks protections: a mandatory procurement route for paid tools, P65.
units.anchor: The tool must be purchased through Procurement

units.why: Contract review lets the university "attach or negotiate AI, privacy, security, and intellectual property terms", institutional review of AI contracts, P65.
units.anchor: attach or negotiate AI, privacy, security, and intellectual property terms

units.why: The stated goal is "to ensure that the University community benefits from AI innovation while maintaining compliance", an institution-wide statement of purpose, P56.
units.anchor: benefits from AI innovation while maintaining compliance
units.frag_start: The goal of this guidance is

notes: Single IT guidance document with no academic-integrity rule of its own. Provost working-group report inaccessible.
